unlisted_practices: Legislators should clarify the residual Class I boundary for medical device software.
The Commission and MDCG should reflect the IMDRF N81 risk characterization considerations in implementation material for software classification.

The Commission and MDCG should specify evidence-quality and weighting criteria for scientific literature and non-clinical evidence, using common specifications where uniform technical rules are needed.
The Commission and Notified Bodies should establish an integrated advice-and-review plan for innovative devices, with published eligibility criteria and performance metrics.

The Commission and MDCG should provide guidance on implementing predetermined change control plans and define the evidence, monitoring, and reassessment triggers for software changes outside an agreed plan.
The Commission, MDCG and competent authorities should establish a harmonized regulatory sandbox plan.
Legislators and the Commission should require risk-proportionate oversight and substantive institutional control for in-house medical devices.
Legislators and the Commission should link device identifiers, AI-enabled device categories, certificates, clinical evidence, software versions, intended purpose, and post-market changes in EUDAMED.
The Commission and MDCG should clarify responsibility and conformity-assessment boundaries for orchestrated and agentic AI systems.
The Commission and Member States should publish a coordinated regulatory map and named authority pathways for products subject to multiple EU frameworks.
Regulators should allow clinically relevant evidence generated through regulatory sandboxes to count as clinical data.
The Notified Body should be able to participate in the expert panel's discussions for innovative device pathways.
Regulators should retain the public declaration requirement for in-house devices under Article 5(5)(e).

screen.reason: Commentary discussing regulatory reform (EU MDR) and policy/governance implications for AI-enabled medical devices.
